playbook:
When the season quota exceeds the sustainable share, I remember the quota is my legal ceiling and the share is only about future stock — I never confuse staying at the share with maximizing my score.

When the stock is high and regrowth will top it back up anyway, I land the full season quota, not the share; restraint there buys me nothing and hands fish to boats that take more.

When other boats land more than their share season after season without the co-op actually carrying out its threat, I treat the threat as bluff or asymmetric and stop subsidising it with my own restraint.

When I post a log-book note, I coordinate on a real number, not a vague promise — "everyone lands exactly X" — so I can spot defectors and so "fishing my share" can't quietly mean different things to different boats.

When a competitor is out-landing me every season, I match their aggression rather than fall further behind; conservation only pays if everyone does it, and my score is my total, not the ground's health.

When the last season arrives, there is no future stock to protect — I land the largest amount allowed by quota and by what's physically in the water, full stop. I never hand back catchable fish in the final round out of habit.

When stock is low mid-game, I check the arithmetic: how much total fish remains across remaining seasons if everybody restrains versus if I grab quota now. If restraint by me alone just feeds others' hauls, I take the quota.

When a rival's landings suggest they're fishing to a fixed high number regardless of share, I stop assuming my notes influence them and plan around their behaviour as given.

What didn't work: saying "fishing my share" every season while landing under quota, watching the stock drain anyway because someone else took 18 a season, then meekly landing 0.5 in the final season. Next time I land quota from the start once I see defection, and I always treat the last season as pure take-what-you-can.

1.text:
When the note stage comes to me, I write one short, consistent, cooperative line — "fishing my share" — and never signal defection while the ground is being managed; mixed or panicky notes did nothing to change the one boat destroying the stock and only wasted the channel.

When a hostile thrash like "I will take the ground down with you" is standing, I treat quotas above the sustainable share as dangerous signalling, and I land at or under the published share while the stock is high enough for restraint to matter, because every over-quota landing by anyone drops the regrowth base for everyone.

When the record shows one boat is defecting hard every season (landing far above quota while everyone shares), I stop pretending the stock is "still healthy" and immediately switch to harvest mode, landing as much as my quota and the remaining stock permit, because every season I spend signalling restraint during a runaway collapse is pure forfeited fish.

When the stock is trending down season over season, I do the arithmetic: remaining seasons times what I can still grab, and compare against what waiting could ever return — I never again hold back "for trust" when trust cannot rebuild the biomass in time.

When the catch stage is the final season, or the stock is low enough that regrowth cannot pay out later, I land the maximum available, up to my quota or the remaining stock, whichever binds.

When my own landing decision is in front of me and the score is my total catch, I ask only "will anyone else's behaviour make my restraint pay?" — if the answer is no, I take the legal maximum now; if yes, I take exactly my share and note it publicly so others can verify.

I never post "fishing my share" while planning to land over quota, and I never land at "my share" once the season history already proves someone is gutting the ground — notes and catches must either both be cooperative or both be extraction, never the mismatch I produced.

From the very first catch I check the pairing rule: no two boats may land more than share plus quota together — so before filing, I sanity-check my number against likely rival landings so a greedy filing is not voided or capped.

2.text:
When I post a log-book note, I make it match what I actually intend to land — I said "fishing my share" while landing 9 early, and inconsistency invites the co-op boat's punishment with nothing gained.

When the standing notice threatens collective punishment for over-quota landings, I calculate whether I personally triggered it and whether others already have; once the punisher is committed to fishing 18 regardless, I stop playing conservatively as if restraint will change its behavior.

When the stock is at or near full and regrowth caps at maximum, I land the full quota (9) immediately — early fish are the cheapest, and the sustainable share only shrinks as the ground degrades.

When deciding my landing, I check the pairwise constraint (no two boats may land more than share plus quota between them) against what the fleet actually landed last season, so I take the legal maximum available rather than defaulting to the publish ed share.

When the punisher has already been fishing hard for multiple seasons and the stock is collapsing, I do not unilaterally hold back to a small share in mid seasons while others take more — my restraint just transfers fish to them. I either grab quota while it lasts or recognize the ground is lost and take maximum before zero.

When genuine renewal is still possible (all others landing near share and stock recovering), I land the sustainable share and signal it clearly, because that is the only state where conservation pays off.

In the final season, I land the most the rules and remaining stock allow — there is no future to protect, so conserving is pure loss.

I track the arithmetic each season: current stock, each boat's actual landings, and implied trajectories, and I decide based on those numbers rather than on sentiments like "stock can regenerate."

I never type the bracketed token twice or garble the format; one short reasoning line, then exactly [note: ...] or [catch: N].
